frontier.hypothesis: Making the const-1 pseudo SINGLE-set gives `li val,1` the birthing bonus too; with both loop-top insns at max_priority the tie falls to INSN_LUID and the target's order (`addu` first) is restored without touching `idx` at all — so the AA shape's `idx = idx2 + idx` could be replaced by a third-variable sum (CA's operand order) and reach 0.
frontier.mechanism: sched.c adjust_priority raises any birthing insn to max_priority; the AA .sched dump shows that when two ready insns are both at 7f000001 the later one is picked first and therefore emitted last. The obstacle is loop.c: a single-set `val = 1;` inside the inner loop is a movable and move_movables hoists it into a fresh callee-save (81 insns, measured in session 1), so the shape must fail exactly one of move_movables' preconditions (m->cond, m->global, or the register-pressure threshold at loop.c:532) while keeping reg_n_sets == 1.
frontier.next_probe: Read move_movables' preconditions and rejection paths in tools/gcc-2.7.2/loop.c, dump t.i.loop for the current AA build (tmp/grind/func_800645B0/s2/dumpAA.py already produces it) to see which tests the current const-1 passes, then construct C shapes that fail exactly one; sandbox each against the CA shape (third-variable sum), where the operand order and every register are already correct.

frontier.hypothesis: A fold-surviving second set of `idx` exists that is NOT the *3 sum and NOT the byte offset, so the sum can take a third-variable destination (CA's correct operand order and register assignment) while the loop top stays right.
frontier.mechanism: birthing_insn_p only needs reg_n_sets[idx] > 1 with a set that survives to flow; the constraint is only that the value must not already be live in another pseudo, and that the set must not turn `idx` into the carrier of the byte offset (which flips local_alloc's $s0 claim).
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate values in this function that are genuinely derived from the slot index and not already computed: e.g. the bit mask recomputed from `idx` in the found-slot arm, the next-slot index used by the loop, or a restructured inner loop that recomputes `i + j` for the occupancy test only. Sandbox each; reject any whose second assignment is dead, unread, or has no reading as ordinary program logic (note the recompute axis is already dead at 79 insns via sweep12).

frontier.hypothesis: The whole loop-top region can be sidestepped by changing which insns land in the inner-loop basic block (e.g. a for-loop spelling where `j++` sits at the loop bottom), which changes what reorg.c has available to steal into the back-edge delay slot.
frontier.mechanism: reorg.c steals the FIRST insn of the target block into the back-edge delay slot; the scheduler decides which insn that is. Changing the block's membership changes the candidate set independently of any priority lever. NB the BANNED construct for this function is the specific relocation of `j += 1;` to between `idx = i + j;` and `val = 1;`; a loop-form change must be justified as a loop form, not as a statement relocation, and must be measured for all of the loop's shapes rather than picked from a directed sweep.
frontier.next_probe: Measure the canonical `for (i = 0; i < 0xF; i += 4)` / `for (j = 0; j < 4; j++)` spelling of the same loops on top of the AA body, and record which basic block each of `addu idx,i,j`, `li val,1` and `addiu j,j,1` lands in via the t.i.sched dump — the point is the block-membership fact, which is reusable regardless of the score.
